svg.text: 09 · Failure handling — every failure, the mechanism that absorbs it, and what is deliberately NOT handled
Left: what can break. Right: the seven mechanisms. An arrow means 'this mechanism is what turns that failure into a delay instead of a loss or a duplicate'.
FAILURES · ordered by how often they happen in production
each was either provoked by a test or reasoned about in DESIGN.md §failure modes
MECHANISMS · seven, all in the store or the gateway
none needs a coordinator, a broker, a heartbeat service or a cache
the largest external dependency; rate limits are normal, not exceptional
one tenant's demand exceeds its share and the queue
agentd pod killed mid-step (deploy, OOM, node loss)
the in-memory step is lost; the lease is orphaned
worker paused: GC, SIGSTOP, network partition
a zombie that later tries to write stale history
the same run:step:i arrives twice at the gateway
gateway dies between side effect and journal write
outcome genuinely unknown; MUST NOT be retried blindly
poison agent: loops on tool calls / tokens
a prompt-injected or buggy agent spending without limit
sandbox runaway: fork bomb, memory, infinite loop
model-authored code doing what model-authored code does
every in-flight transaction aborts at once
the running cluster no longer matches the reviewed state
the run stays QUEUED; a delay, never a loss
the ENTIRE failure detector; ≤ TTL 30 s + 3 s
owner = me AND not expired AND next_seq = expected
a stale writer gets ErrLeaseLost, writes nothing
INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on run:step:i
sandbox limits enforced by the parent
killCgroup: every pid, not just the child
HPA 2–40 workers; Argo reverts drift, prunes extras
The production step, if it were needed
the model is told 'MAY OR MAY NOT have taken effect' and must verify before retrying
end-to-end idempotency keys in the third-party API (Stripe-style) — not something the platform can promise
loss of the Postgres primary AND its replicas
runs since the last backup are gone; the audit chain has a hole that VerifyChain reports
PITR + cross-region replica; the design's tiering to object storage makes cold history independent of the
a kernel LPE from inside a namespace sandbox
PoC: host compromise (namespace driver shares the kernel)
production driver: gVisor RuntimeClass + tainted pool + no SA token + default-deny — the escape lands
N replicas each admit a full share: up to N× over-admission of the provider budget
Redis-backed buckets with a local lease (the documented gap; interface already isolates the limiter)
we do not try: a clever injection is indistinguishable from a legitimate instruction
containment is the product: allowlists, no network, no credential in the sandbox, human approval for
